hero.kicker: GIS production · Spatial analysis · Workflow automation
hero.headline: Urban planner. Geospatial technical lead.
hero.statement: For four years I ran delivery at a geospatial consultancy, leading a team of about ten that mapped 1.5 million+ land parcels across 35–40 cities on five continents. I designed the delivery system and its automations, hired and trained the team, and handled client communications.
hero.intro: Currently a GIS Associate at Artelia Consulting Engineers, on APIIC's BHAVYA scheme projects. Next, I want the statistical and machine-learning depth to move from production mapping to spatial modelling.

experience.title: Experience
experience.intro: Four years at Planning Saga, a geospatial consultancy, where I moved from GIS Associate to Senior Associate & Technical Lead within nine months, and to Operations & Development Lead just over two years in. Since September 2026 I have been a GIS Associate at Artelia Consulting Engineers, working on site at APIIC as my team's key point of contact for projects under the BHAVYA scheme.

anchor.summary: One long-running engagement: plot-level land-parcel data for a global metaverse real-estate platform, usually with several cities in production at once. The founding partner led the firm from the Netherlands while pursuing higher studies there; on the ground in India, I ran the production system, day-to-day operations, the team and the client relationship.

pillars.title: Delivery system
points: Designed and refined a 10-stage GIS delivery framework with QA gates at neighbourhood and city level
Wrote the workflow procedures for every stage, plus city-preparation protocols and post-delivery retrospectives
Researched local property prices for every city, so the price per square foot (or local unit) we used stayed close to real market rates

pillars.title: Automation & tooling
points: Built a script layer integrated with the GIS workflow for checks, data extraction, API calls, cleaning, formatting to client spec and automated QA
Replaced manual address extraction (1.5 h per 1,000 parcels) with a fixed ~15-minute automated run, applied across 1M+ parcels
Built a capacity & deadline model that forecast city finish dates to ~95% accuracy

pillars.title: Team & operations
points: Owned hiring end to end: sourcing, technical screening, assignment-based evaluation and about 100 interviews
Built onboarding and training and ran performance reviews: 20+ people over four years, with a core team of about 10
Ran planning and allocation in ClickUp: city-as-project structure, stage checklists, dashboards and time tracking
Wrote the operating documentation: workflow processes, technology, administrative and hiring processes, and user manuals for every automation and tool we built

pillars.title: Client & growth
points: Primary client liaison for 3+ years, with weekly progress and strategy reporting
Drafted the pre-final client–consultant service agreement, including its legal terms
Involved in business development: market research and stakeholder interviews on where the practice could grow

work.title: Selected work
work.intro: The role I held longest, my B.Plan thesis and an internship project, each with a map or tool you can try.

items.title: Engineering a city-scale parcel-mapping practice
items.summary: The delivery system, automation and planning behind 1.5M+ attributed parcels across 35–40 cities, from running production and the team to owning the client relationship. Includes a working recreation of my capacity & deadline model.

items.title: Earthquake-triggered landslide hazard in Aizawl
items.summary: Two multi-criteria indices, landslide hazard and earthquake vulnerability, overlaid across Aizawl district to set a priority tehsil and a relief plan for Aizawl city. Rebuilt as a live model you can re-weight, with a look back at what the rebuild showed.

items.title: Spatial patterns of road-crash fatalities in Mumbai
items.summary: 1,681 fatal crashes (2017–2020) analysed across Mumbai's 24 wards in ArcGIS and Excel. Pedestrians made up 47% of road-user fatalities in 2018–20. The 2021 layers can now be explored on an interactive map.

approach.title: How I use AI
approach.intro: I draft the idea, the intent and the flow; AI does most of the execution. Before anything is used, I check what comes out against real data.

items.title: Code & automation
items.body: Python, Apps Script and API pipelines: I designed the logic and the flow, AI wrote most of the code, and I tested it against real data before it went near production. At Planning Saga the automation layer (checks, data pulls, API calls, cleaning, formatting to client spec, QA) and the capacity & deadline model were built this way.

items.title: Tools, end to end
items.body: Tools I designed and AI built: a local Node.js CV editor, this portfolio (including its map engine and data pipeline), plugins and add-ons for software I use daily, and personal quality-of-life tools such as custom apps for my e-readers, desktop organisers, and maintenance scripts for my photo and media libraries.

items.title: Systems & documentation
items.body: Workflow procedures, training material, client reports, proposals and a service-agreement draft. I set out what each needed, AI helped structure and draft, and I wrote and checked the final versions.

items.title: Research & fast learning
items.body: Getting productive quickly in new methods and tools, and desk research for business development and new markets.

approach.principle: I set the idea and the flow, AI executes, and data decides. Every output gets checked against something independent: a published total, a hand-checked sample, or a QA gate.
approach.principleExample: Example: the capacity & deadline model for city projects. I designed its four sections, the rules and the benchmarks; AI wrote the formula logic. I then checked its dates against actual completions, where it held to about 95%.
approach.note: For context: everything before Planning Saga, including my B.Plan thesis, studio work and internships such as WRI India, predates these tools and was done without AI.
